Bound a comparison under every allocation of unknown-ethnicity stops

Source: R/sensitivity.R
btg_sensitivity.Rd

The recorded stop-rate ratio leaves out stops whose ethnicity was not recorded. This function reports the range the ratio would take if every one of those stops belonged to the compared group, or every one of them to the White group, which are the two extreme allocations. Any allocation of the unknown stops between the groups gives a ratio inside that range, and allocating them in the same proportions as the recorded stops leaves the ratio unchanged. For force-level datasets the function also reports the best and worst rank a force could hold if every force's unknown stops were allocated in its favour or against it.

Usage

btg_sensitivity(x, year = NULL, group = NULL)

Arguments

x

A comparison dataset from btg_get_data(): force_disparity, force_ethnicity_year or council_ethnicity_year.

year

Optional single calendar year to keep. NULL keeps every year in the selection.

group

Optional single ethnic group to keep. NULL keeps every group in the selection.

Value

A data frame with one row per area, year and group: the recorded counts, unknown_share (unknown-ethnicity stops as a share of all records), the recorded ratio with its Poisson interval, ratio_min (every unknown stop assigned to White), ratio_max (every unknown stop assigned to the compared group) and parity_direction: "above" when the whole range exceeds 1, "below" when it is entirely under 1, and "sensitive" when the side of parity depends on the unknown stops. Force rows add eligible, rank, rank_best, rank_worst (ranks among the forces eligible in the recorded data, under the most favourable and least favourable allocations) and the coverage columns. Missing returns remain missing. The attributes dataset and release identify the evidence.

Details

The sampling interval and the allocation range answer different questions and are deliberately not combined. The interval conditions on the recorded counts; the range conditions on nothing about the unknown stops except their number. Neither captures missing monthly returns, classification differences between officer-defined and Census ethnicity, or the choice of resident populations as the exposure measure, and neither establishes discrimination. Council rows carry no rank or eligibility, as in the dataset.

Examples

s <- btg_sensitivity(btg_get_data())
head(s[c("force_label", "ratio", "ratio_min", "ratio_max", "parity_direction")])
#>        force_label    ratio ratio_min ratio_max parity_direction
#> 1          Norfolk 9.971068  9.616471 13.788563            above
#> 2 Devon & Cornwall 9.748324  9.336930 20.940844            above
#> 3      West Mercia 9.673905  9.134508 16.137257            above
#> 4           Sussex 9.461250  9.338614 10.414488            above
#> 5           Surrey 8.612550  8.419686  9.743609            above
#> 6           Dorset 8.217899  6.250789 51.673153            above
table(s$parity_direction, useNA = "ifany")
#> 
#> above  <NA> 
#>    40     4 

y <- btg_get_data("force_ethnicity_year", years = 2025, groups = "Asian")
head(btg_sensitivity(y)[c("force_label", "rank", "rank_best", "rank_worst")])
#>       force_label rank rank_best rank_worst
#> 1     West Mercia    1         1         11
#> 2 North Yorkshire    2         2         24
#> 3   Staffordshire    3         1         30
#> 4  West Yorkshire    4         2         29
#> 5         Cumbria    5         1         32
#> 6 South Yorkshire    6         1         31
